title: Maximum Entropy of Sums of Independent Ternary Random Variables
summary: The classical problem of maximizing the Shannon entropy of a sum of independent random variables supported on a finite alphabet is considered and settled in the ternary case. Namely, the following theorem is established: if \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are independent random variables taking values in \(\{0,1,2\}\), then the entropy of \(S_n=X_1+\cdots+X_n\) is maximized when \(X_1,\ldots,X_{n-1}\) are uniform on \(\{0,2\}\) and the probability mass function of \(X_n\) is given by \(\Prob(X_n=0) = \Prob(X_n=2) = w/2\), \(\Prob(X_n=1) = 1-w\), where \(w = \big(1 + 2^{-H(B_n)+H(B_{n-1})}\big)^{-1}\) and…
